Outbound Comms Grounding

No grounding block, no draft. Every outbound message gets read-and-proved against the knowledge base first.
SKILL · RUNS AUTOMATICALLY WHEN IT APPLIES

What it does

Before a message goes to another human being, this skill finds out what the knowledge base already knows about that recipient and that situation - and proves it read it. It emits a KB GROUNDING block with file paths and line-numbered verbatim quotes before any draft text. If there is no grounding block, there is no draft.

It also locks the domain so standards from one part of Adam's life never leak into another. Work and civic writing have different voices, different sourcing, and different consequences; applying the wrong one is worse than citing nothing at all.

Why it exists

Four times, a draft was written from the model's own priors and then labelled with an attribution line naming a knowledge base module that was never opened. The last one went out before the gap was caught.

The knowledge base was never the problem - the right module described that exact scenario. What was missing was any point in the drafting path where a read had to happen. Writing prose needs no tool call, so there is no natural checkpoint. Three earlier attempts to fix this with prompt rules all failed for that reason. The line-numbered quote is the fix: it cannot be produced from memory.

The procedure

  • 1. Classify - recipient class, relationship temperature, purpose, and domain, each stated in one line before anything is opened. Classification first, because a friendly note from an official and a hostile public comment share every keyword and need opposite handling.
  • 2. Lock the domain - pick exactly one, declared up front. The domain sets an allowlist of knowledge base paths; anything outside it is not read, not cited, and not applied.
  • 3. Read the curated lookup in full - the whole index-lookup file, no head, no grep, no line limits. A truncated read silently misses modules.
  • 4. Shortlist by "use when" text, then read - matching on how a situation is described, not on topic nouns. Expect one to three modules, and pull both substance (what to say) and relational craft (how to say it to this recipient).
  • 5. Keyword search only as a fallback - and treated as weak evidence. Search-first routing was tested and failed to surface the correct module; the curated "use when" lines matched perfectly.

Domain locking

Each domain allows a specific set of paths and blocks the rest. Three crossovers must never happen, in severity order:

CrossoverWhy it matters
Civic-action content in a work messageHighest severity - stop the line. An organizing frame inside a customer email creates professional and political exposure Adam did not choose.
Sales and marketing persuasion patterns in a civic messageA sales-sequence structure inside an advocacy post discredits the campaign.
Work or civic register in a family or personal messageWrong voice entirely for the relationship.

When the domain is ambiguous, it asks rather than guessing. This is the one place where refusing to act is always right - "most likely work" is not a domain lock. Dual-domain topics (surveillance technology, student data privacy, school safety) default conservative: anything going to a work address, customer, vendor or colleague is work, always. Cross-domain reads need explicit permission in that same turn and get recorded in the grounding block; the skill never self-authorizes.

What the grounding block looks like

KB GROUNDING - read this turn
DOMAIN: civic-action | RECIPIENT: public official, friendly inbound
ALLOWED: adam/civic-action/**, adam/writing-craft/**
adam/civic-action/.../module-07-warm-1on1-official-engagement.md
  L44: "<sentence copied verbatim from the file>"
  L91: "<sentence copied verbatim from the file>"
APPLIED:
  L44 -> answering warmly without conceding the ordinance position
  L91 -> proposing a 1:1 rather than waiting for public comment

One module minimum, two line-numbered verbatim quotes per module, and an APPLIED line tying each quote to a real choice in the draft. The block stays in chat - it never goes inside the text you copy and send. If a read fails, the skill reports GROUNDING FAILED - no draft produced and offers three options rather than quietly drafting anyway.

Things that quietly break it

  • A read earlier in the same conversation does not count. Re-read per draft. Reusing the memory of an earlier read is exactly how the last failure happened.
  • Never invent a quote or a line number. A wrong module is recoverable. A fabricated receipt destroys the whole mechanism.
  • Banned phrases - "Grounded in [module]" with no quotes, "per best practices", "based on the KB", "drawing on [topic] research". Each asserts grounding while carrying none, and their interchangeability with real citations is what kept four weeks of failures invisible.

Composing with other skills

This skill supplies the front half - the grounded read. Formatting skills supply the back half, and none of them performs a knowledge base read of its own, so this runs first. Help-center articles go on to help-center-article; support and Salesforce email to salesforce-email-template-builder; internal STA comms to internal-comms. Facebook posts, texts, letters and public comments need no formatting skill.

When to use it

Any time a message is being written to another person, even a short one, and even when the knowledge base is not mentioned. Not for summarizing or analyzing an inbound message when no reply is being written.

How to trigger it

"draft a reply"

"respond to this email"

"write a post about..."

"how should I answer this"

or just paste an inbound email, screenshot, or message and ask what to say
